key_insight: Validation-driven bilevel optimization tunes mesh-free PDE solver designs, while error analysis connects approximate hypergradients and validation residuals to solution accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The framework provides a unified way to tune representation, residual weighting, and regularization across multiple mesh-free solver classes.
method: Fit trial coefficients on training collocation residuals; tune solver-design parameters on held-out validation residuals.
Approximate nonlinear lower-level solutions with finite, warm-started damped Gauss–Newton updates.
Use the damped Gauss–Newton matrix to initialize and precondition adjoint iterations, with bounds separating key approximation errors.
evidence_signal: Experiments on several nonlinear PDEs, including a high-dimensional problem, report accuracy and efficiency across Kansa, random-feature/extreme-learning-machine, and physics-informed neural network solvers; the abstract gives no numerical metrics.
watch_item: Hypergradient bounds are local, and translating validation residuals into solution-error guarantees depends on sampling bounds and residual stability.
paper_title: A Validation-Driven Bilevel Optimization Method for Mesh-Free PDE Solvers and Its Error Analysis
